cotes-de-provence-rose.name: Côtes de Provence Rosé
cotes-de-provence-rose.summary: The modern Provence benchmark is pale, dry and refreshing, built around delicate fruit rather than red-wine weight.

style.label: Rosé · Pale Mediterranean style
style.method: Direct pressing or brief skin maceration, followed by cool white-wine-style fermentation
style.effect: Short skin contact limits tannin and color while preserving fresh red-fruit, citrus and floral aromas.

provence-rose-blend.expect: Pale, dry and delicate, with fresh strawberry, peach and citrus carried by crisp acidity.

identity.setting: Warm Mediterranean coast and inland hills
identity.terrain: Varied limestone and crystalline Provençal landscapes
identity.soil: Limestone, schist and crystalline soils depending on subzone

why.cause: Gentle pressing or very short skin contact
why.effect: Keeps color pale and tannin low while capturing delicate red-fruit aromas.

why.cause: Warm sun balanced by wind and coastal influence
why.effect: Supports ripe fruit while retaining the refreshing profile expected of Provence rosé.

tavel-rose.name: Tavel
tavel-rose.summary: Tavel is a deliberately deeper and more structured Rhône rosé, built for the table rather than maximum delicacy.

style.label: Rosé · Fuller Rhône style
style.method: Rosé vinification with more extraction and color than the palest Mediterranean styles
style.effect: Greater skin-derived structure gives a fuller, more savory rosé that can handle substantial food.

grenache.decant: No decant; 10 min air for richer examples
grenache.expect: Deeper and fuller than pale Provence rosé, with ripe red fruit, herbs and enough structure for a meal.

identity.terrain: Terraces and slopes west of the Rhône near Avignon
identity.soil: Limestone, sand, clay and rounded stones

why.cause: More extraction than very pale rosé styles
why.effect: Builds body, color and savory structure rather than aiming only for delicacy.
Push ripe red-fruit character while the Mistral helps retain freshness.

navarra-rosado.name: Navarra Rosado
navarra-rosado.summary: Navarra's long rosado tradition gives Garnacha a vivid, fruit-driven expression with freshness and more color than the palest Provence model.

style.label: Rosado · Garnacha sangrado style
style.method: Traditionally made from free-run or bled must after short contact with red-grape skins
style.effect: The method preserves vivid Garnacha fruit and color while keeping tannin modest and acidity refreshing.

grenache.expect: Bright and juicy, with strawberry and cherry, refreshing acidity and a vivid pink color.

identity.setting: Northern Spain where Atlantic, continental and Mediterranean influences meet
identity.soil: Diverse limestone, clay and alluvial soils across subzones

why.cause: Garnacha plus traditional sangrado/free-run rosado methods
why.effect: Emphasizes juicy red fruit and vivid color without red-wine tannin.

why.cause: Navarra's mix of cooler and warmer subzones
why.effect: Helps balance generous fruit with the freshness that defines the region's rosados.

collio-oslavia-orange.name: Collio / Oslavia — Skin-contact Ribolla
collio-oslavia-orange.summary: Long skin contact can turn Ribolla Gialla from a crisp white into an amber, textural wine with tea-like tannin and savory depth.

style.label: Orange / amber · Long skin contact
style.method: Extended maceration of white Ribolla Gialla on its skins, a style strongly associated with Oslavia
style.effect: Skin contact adds amber color, phenolic grip and tea-like savory complexity while Ribolla's acidity keeps the wine fresh.

ribolla-gialla.expect: Dry and grippy, with dried citrus, apricot, tea and savory notes over firm acidity.

identity.setting: Alpine-Adriatic hills on Italy's Slovenian border
identity.soil: Ponca / flysch of marl and sandstone
influences: Local tradition of long Ribolla maceration

why.effect: Extracts color and tannin that ordinary white-wine pressing leaves behind.
Keeps a structured, phenolic orange wine energetic rather than heavy.

kakheti-qvevri-amber.name: Kakheti — Qvevri Amber
kakheti-qvevri-amber.summary: Traditional Kakhetian qvevri winemaking gives Rkatsiteli an amber color, firm tannic texture and savory dried-fruit complexity.

style.label: Amber / orange · Qvevri skin contact
style.method: White grapes ferment and mature in buried qvevri with extended contact with skins and other grape solids
style.effect: Long contact extracts amber color and tannin, creating a structured white-grape wine with tea, dried-fruit and herbal character.

rkatsiteli.expect: Amber, dry and structured, with dried fruit, tea, herbs and noticeable tannic grip from extended qvevri skin contact.

identity.setting: Warm continental valley with Caucasus mountain influence
influences: Extended skin contact for traditional amber wines

why.cause: Fermentation and ageing with skins in qvevri
why.effect: Adds tannin, amber color and savory complexity to a white grape.
Provides the freshness needed to balance the wine's unusually firm texture.

cremant-bourgogne.name: Crémant de Bourgogne
cremant-bourgogne.summary: Bourgogne sparkling wine in Chardonnay-led blanc de blancs and Pinot Noir-led blanc de noirs expressions.

style.label: Sparkling · Blanc de blancs · Brut
style.method: Traditional method: second fermentation in bottle, lees ageing and disgorgement
style.effect: This profile models a Chardonnay-led blanc de blancs; other permitted white varieties may occur. Lees contact can add bread and nut notes; dosage, producer and ageing change the final style.

chardonnay.decant: No decant; pour gently to preserve bubbles
chardonnay.ageing: Usually ready on release; drink within 1–3 years for freshness
chardonnay.expect: Fresh and citrus-led, with orchard fruit, fine bubbles and a light bread-like note.

style.label: Sparkling · Blanc de noirs · Brut
style.method: Traditional method: second fermentation in bottle, lees ageing and disgorgement
style.effect: This profile models a Pinot Noir-led white sparkling wine; Gamay may also be included. It is not a still red wine. Lees contact can add bread and nut notes; dosage, producer and ageing change the final style.

pinot-noir.decant: No decant; pour gently to preserve bubbles
pinot-noir.ageing: Usually ready on release; drink within 1–3 years for freshness
pinot-noir.expect: A fuller white sparkling expression of Pinot Noir, with orchard fruit, subtle berry notes and savory breadth.

identity.terrain: Slopes across the Bourgogne appellation area
identity.soil: Varied soils with a substantial clay-limestone component

why.effect: Retains freshness for a sparkling base wine.

why.cause: Second fermentation in bottle and time on lees
why.effect: Creates bubbles and can contribute bread-like texture and aromas.

cremant-alsace.name: Crémant d’Alsace
cremant-alsace.summary: Alsace sparkling styles include a Pinot Blanc-led white expression and a Pinot Noir rosé.

style.label: Sparkling · Pinot Blanc-led · Brut
style.method: Traditional method: second fermentation in bottle, lees ageing and disgorgement
style.effect: Pinot Blanc is a major white base; Auxerrois, Chardonnay, Riesling, Pinot Gris and Pinot Noir can also contribute to white cuvées. Lees contact can add bread and nut notes; dosage, producer and ageing change the final style.

pinot-blanc.decant: No decant; pour gently to preserve bubbles
pinot-blanc.ageing: Usually ready on release; drink within 1–3 years for freshness
pinot-blanc.expect: Supple orchard fruit, fresh bubbles and gentle floral notes in a dry white sparkling style.

style.label: Sparkling · Rosé · Brut
style.method: Traditional method: second fermentation in bottle, lees ageing and disgorgement
style.effect: Crémant d’Alsace rosé is made from Pinot Noir. White cuvées have a different range of permitted grapes. Lees contact can add bread and nut notes; dosage, producer and ageing change the final style.

pinot-noir.decant: No decant; pour gently to preserve bubbles
pinot-noir.ageing: Usually ready on release; drink within 1–3 years for freshness
pinot-noir.expect: Dry and lively rosé bubbles with red-berry fruit, light structure and a fresh finish.

identity.terrain: Vosges foothills and sheltered vineyard slopes
identity.soil: Diverse limestone, marl, granite and sandstone soils

why.effect: Retains freshness for a sparkling base wine.

why.cause: Second fermentation in bottle and time on lees
why.effect: Creates bubbles and can contribute bread-like texture and aromas.

cremant-loire.name: Crémant de Loire
cremant-loire.summary: Chenin-led white sparkling wine from the Loire, with a range of permitted blending varieties.

style.label: Sparkling · Chenin-led white · Brut
style.method: Traditional method: second fermentation in bottle, lees ageing and disgorgement
style.effect: This is a Chenin-led white expression, sometimes blended with Chardonnay or other permitted grapes. It does not represent every permitted blend or the rosé style. Lees contact can add bread and nut notes; dosage, producer and ageing change the final style.

chenin-blanc.decant: No decant; pour gently to preserve bubbles
chenin-blanc.ageing: Usually ready on release; drink within 1–3 years for freshness
chenin-blanc.expect: Brisk apple and citrus, a touch of quince and a fine savory finish, with pronounced freshness.

identity.terrain: Anjou, Saumur and Touraine vineyard landscapes
identity.soil: Varied limestone, tuffeau, schist, gravel and clay soils

why.effect: Retains freshness for a sparkling base wine.

why.cause: Second fermentation in bottle and time on lees
why.effect: Creates bubbles and can contribute bread-like texture and aromas.
